titulo: Effect of continuous-use air sterilization on healthcare-associated infections in a neonatal intensive care unit: A quasi-experimental study
tituloEs: Esterilización continua del aire no reduce infecciones asociadas a atención en UCIN
resumenOriginal: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a significant challenge in NICUs. Continuous air sterilization systems may reduce environmental microbial contamination, but their impact on HAIs and multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) colonization remains uncertain. To evaluate the association of a continuous air sterilization system with healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) colonization, and environmental microbial burden in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). This quasi-experimental pre-post intervention study was conducted in a Level III NICU of a tertiary care hospital in Southern India. Neonates admitted during a 5-month pre-intervention phase were compared with those admitted during a 5-month post-intervention phase following installation of the continuous air sterilization system, with a 1-month washout period excluded from analysis. Primary outcomes were definite and probable HAIs. Secondary outcomes included MDRO colonization, environmental microbial burden, antibiotic utilization, and sepsis-related clinical outcomes. Crude effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals were additionally calculated; multivariable logistic regression was used for colonization outcomes to account for baseline differences. Among 698 neonates, 367 were included in the pre-intervention and 331 in the post-intervention cohort. The post-intervention cohort had significantly lower birth weight (2520 ± 771 vs. 2398 ± 820 g; p = 0.043) and gestational age (36 ± 3 vs. 35 ± 4 weeks; p = 0.0003). The incidence of definite HAI (5.2% vs. 6.3%; p = 0.611), probable HAI (2.5% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.094), and any HAI (7.4% vs. 9.7%; p = 0.332) did not differ significantly between the groups. After adjustment for gestational age and birth weight, the odds of any HAI remained similar (aOR 1.05, 95% CI 0.58-1.91). New MDRO colonization was also comparable (6.0% vs. 7.0%; p = 0.713). However, the intervention was associated with a significant reduction in airborne microbial burden. Conclusions: The continuous air sterilization system was associated with a substantial reduction in airborne microbial burden; however, no statistically significant reduction in HAIs or MDRO colonization was observed. Given the uncontrolled pre-post design and baseline differences, causal effects on clinical outcomes remain unproven. This study was only powered to detect very large effects; therefore, clinical benefit should be tested in larger cluster-randomized studies, or in settings where airborne transmission is a major driver of HAI. What is already known • Environmental microbial contamination contributes to the transmission of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in NICUs. • Air sterilization technologies can reduce airborne microbial load, but evidence for their impact on neonatal clinical outcomes and HAIs remains limited and inconsistent. What this study adds • Continuous air sterilization was associated with a reduction in environmental microbial burden in a Level III NICU. • Because airborne transmission is one of several routes of NICU infection, trials of air sterilization need either very large samples or settings and endpoints in which airborne infection predominates.

tips.texto: La esterilización continua del aire redujo la carga microbiana ambiental, pero no disminuyó las IAAS ni la colonización por organismos multirresistentes en esta UCIN.

Las IAAS neonatales dependen principalmente de transmisión por contacto y dispositivos invasivos, no de patógenos aéreos. La reducción del aire contaminado puede ser insuficiente para impactar las tasas de infección.
Diferencias basales entre cohortes (menor peso y edad gestacional post intervención) y ausencia de aleatorización impiden establecer causalidad. Los hallazgos deben interpretarse con cautela.

Ante recursos limitados, conviene priorizar intervenciones con evidencia sólida: higiene de manos, paquetes de prevención de infecciones asociadas a catéteres y ventiladores, y políticas de uso prudente de antibióticos.
Se requieren ensayos aleatorizados por conglomerados, con muestras grandes o en contextos donde la transmisión aérea sea predominante, para evaluar el beneficio clínico real de estas tecnologías.

sintesis: Estudio cuasiexperimental en una UCIN de India evaluó el impacto de un sistema de esterilización continua del aire sobre infecciones asociadas a atención (IAAS) y colonización por organismos multirresistentes. Aunque se redujo la carga microbiana ambiental, no hubo diferencias significativas en las IAAS ni en la colonización.
aplicacionDocente: Útil para discutir con residentes la diferencia entre desenlaces microbiológicos (carga ambiental) y clínicos (IAAS). Refuerza la necesidad de evaluar críticamente tecnologías costosas antes de su implementación masiva, especialmente cuando las vías de transmisión predominantes no son aéreas.
disenoEstudio: Estudio cuasiexperimental pre–post intervención en 698 neonatos en una UCIN de nivel III
fraseInfografia: Menos microbios en el aire no siempre significa menos infecciones en neonatos
advertencia: Diseño cuasiexperimental sin aleatorización, con diferencias basales significativas entre cohortes y poder estadístico limitado para detectar efectos moderados.
